technical_and_design_decisions: Externalize protoutil, bccsp, msp, and discovery client packages into a shared library module (e.g., hyperledger/fabric-lib-go) to enable reuse by both Fabric core and fabric-sdk-go.

Refactor chaincode shim packages (statebased and entities) by replacing heavy core dependencies (cauthdsl, protoutil, bccsp, flogging, identity) with lightweight standard library logic or direct protobuf types.
Update the marbles02_private chaincode sample documentation and shell command comments to sanitize line endings across OS environments using 'tr -d \r\n'.
assumptions: Development work will span hyperledger/fabric, hyperledger/fabric-lib-go, and hyperledger/fabric-samples repositories as necessary.
Existing unit and integration test suites are available to validate that refactoring does not break API compatibility or runtime behavior.
CI pipelines allow pushing updated dependency modules and verifying dependency trees using 'go list'.

activities.activity_description: Analyze dependency graphs for chaincode shim packages (statebased and entities) and design the module extraction strategy for protoutil, bccsp, msp, and discovery client.
Refactor core/chaincode/shim/ext/statebased and core/chaincode/shim/ext/entities to eliminate references to bccsp, flogging, cauthdsl, protoutil, and identity, ensuring only proto packages remain.
Extract protoutil utilities to fabric-lib-go/protoutil, update fabric imports, and verify downstream usability for Fabric Go SDK.
Extract BCCSP interfaces, factory, and implementations to a shared external module, updating Fabric core references and tests.
Refactor and extract MSP components to enable external consumption by Go SDK without code duplication.
Migrate the discovery client package to fabric-lib-go/discovery and update Fabric core references.
Update comment instructions and shell export expressions in marbles02_private chaincode to handle newline/carriage return characters across Windows/Linux hosts.
Execute 'go list' dependency checks on shim packages, run full unit/integration test suites across repositories, and verify build stability.
